label: Principal Ideals
subgoals: An ideal in a ring is principal when one element generates it.
The integers and the polynomial ring over a field are the two examples that carry most of the intuition.

label: Gcd and Lcm
subgoals: The ideal generated by two integers is generated by their greatest common divisor.
The intersection of two principal ideals is generated by their least common multiple.

label: The Domain Chain
subgoals: Every Euclidean domain is a principal ideal domain, and every principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain.
The reverse implications fail, so the chain is a one-way supply of theorems.
